title: Current and Trail
premise: Astrid Hartwell, a riverboat captain on the Mekong's northern reaches, owes a dangerous sum to the syndicate that holds her boat's papers. When dying prospector Elias Vane trades her a map to a monsoon-hidden jade cache in exchange for a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter, Astrid expects an easy detour — until the syndicate's enforcer boards her boat and the daughter, Lin, turns out to be running from the same men. Through flood season, sabotage, and a slow-burning love neither can afford, Astrid must choose between paying her debt and keeping her word. In the end she scuttles her own boat to destroy the syndicate's claim, delivers the map to Lin, and walks away with nothing but a compass and, for the first time, someone to share the current with.
about_author: Ines Nystrom is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on Southeast Asian rivers before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. She lives in a houseboat with unreliable plumbing and writes about people who belong to water more than land.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She pilots her aging riverboat the Kestrel through low-season shallows, dodging sandbars and the syndicate collector who reminds her of her debt. Establishes her competence, isolation, and the compass she inherited from her father. Emotional beat: weary self-sufficiency masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A feverish prospector, Elias Vane, collapses aboard at a fueling dock and offers a hand-drawn map to a jade cache if she'll promise to bring it to his daughter in Chiang Saen. Astrid, needing money, agrees but plans to sell the map instead. Emotional beat: guilt taking root beside pragmatism.

chapters.title: Passenger with No Papers
chapters.summary: Lin's POV introduced. She stows away on the Kestrel fleeing the syndicate, who want the map her father carried. Astrid discovers her mid-river; suspicion flares into uneasy truce when they realize they're bound for the same person. Emotional beat: two guarded women testing each other's edges.

chapters.title: What the Syndicate Wants
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The enforcer Dane Rook boards at a checkpoint, searching for Lin and the map. Astrid hides both beneath her engine bilge, lying for the first time in years. They slip past, but Rook marks the Kestrel. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Storm season closes the upper river; the Kestrel takes on water from old seams. Stranded at a flooded village, Astrid and Lin repair the boat together and trade histories — Astrid's dead father, Lin's estranged one. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling in forced stillness.

chapters.title: The Map Is Not the Treasure
chapters.summary: Lin's POV. Lin deciphers her father's annotations and realizes the cache coordinates sit inside syndicate territory — Elias meant it as bait to draw out his old partners, not as a gift. She confronts Astrid about selling the map. Trust fractures. Emotional beat: betrayal and its mirror image.

chapters.title: Rapids
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rook ambushes them at the gorge narrows; a chase through white water wrecks the Kestrel's rudder and nearly drowns Lin. Astrid saves her, and the almost-kiss between them goes unspoken. Emotional beat: love admitted in adrenaline, denied in aftermath.

chapters.title: Debt and Promise
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Rook offers Astrid a clean slate for the map and Lin. Cornered by debt and duty, she pretends to accept while planning otherwise. She finds Elias's final letter revealing he knew she'd choose right. Emotional beat: the quiet resolve of a woman deciding who she is.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Climax: Astrid lures Rook's gunboat into flood-swollen rapids and scuttles the Kestrel against his hull, destroying both the syndicate's leverage and her only home. She and Lin escape downstream as the river swallows everything. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Current and Trail
chapters.summary: Lin's POV. Weeks later, the two reach Chiang Saen and deliver the map — and Elias's letter — to a daughter who finally understands her father. Debt-free but penniless, Astrid signs onto a cargo run as first mate, Lin beside her. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt not around what was lost, but who remains.
